name: Ferrofluid
author: E. T. Carter
description: Magnetic fluid in a dark dish round a steel form. As the field builds the fluid climbs the form in a slow pulse, coating it in rows of sharp spikes, holds near the top, then slides back into the spiked pool, and the bare steel turns into the next form: a spiral spire, an onion bulb, a thick coil, a twisted three-lobed column. Near-black and glossy, with the theme catching only along the spike edges.

sculpture.label: Magnetic fluid climbing a steel form in slow pulses, spiked all over, then sliding off as the steel turns into the next shape.

params.label: Pull
params.effect: How strongly the field raises the spikes; 0 lets the fluid lie smooth on the spire and in the pool.

params.label: Pulse
params.effect: How fast the fluid climbs, falls back and the steel changes form; 0 holds the first form with the fluid at its foot.

params.label: Mouse influence
params.effect: How far the pointer orbits the camera round the piece; 0 ignores the mouse.
